title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-14
content:
Security Eng sync notes - 2026-03-14

Attendees: Aisha Patel (sec), Marcus Lee (platform), Sofia Alvarez (infra), Daniel Kim (SRE), Rachel Nguyen (appsec)

Agenda:
- Quick vuln triage roundup
- Secrets scanning + recent leaked token postmortem follow-up
- Threat modeling: new public embeddings endpoint
- Action items and owners

1) Vulnerability triage (bulk)
- SEC-421 (high): deserialization bug in internal model-messaging service.
  - Reported: 2026-03-11 via fuzzing pipeline.
  - Impact: unauthenticated actor can craft malformed payloads to trigger OOB reads; potential info disclosure.
  - Current status: POC validated by Marcus. Patch branch opened: github PR #987 (linked).
  - Mitigation options discussed: short-term WAF rule to block suspicious payloads + disable untrusted-deserialize flag; long-term: replace custom deserializer with safe-parser (ETA: 2 sprints).
  - Decision: Apply WAF rule today (Marcus), ship hotfix to disable flag asap (Daniel).
  - Open questions: do any external customers rely on current behavior? Product to confirm (Rachel to coordinate).

- SEC-430 (medium): improper validation on model-upload metadata leads to malformed filenames.
  - Low exploitability but causes ingestion failures; backlog item to harden validation.
  - Assigned to Sofia, target end-of-week.

- Misc: two low findings from dependency scan (outdated transitive lib in embedding worker). Sofia to schedule upgrade in next maintenance window.

2) Secrets scanning and leaked token follow-up
- Summary: On 2026-03-10 we detected an exposed service token in a public gist (automated detector). Token belonged to a short-lived CI worker account.
  - Root cause: script in repo had leftover creds in test fixture; token was limited-scoped but allowed access to a non-prod S3 bucket.
  - Response: rotated token, revoked historic tokens for the CI app, and invalidated all runner caches.
  - Remediation items:
    * Backfill: scan all repos for similar fixtures (Sofia + Marcus).
    * Improve pre-commit hooks and CI check: add rule to fail on fixture-like tokens and deny commits that include 'TEST_TOKEN' patterns (Daniel).
    * Secrets scanning telemetry: tune detector to reduce false positives and add severity scoring (Aisha).
  - Timeline: rotation complete; scan/backfill in progress with 48h SLA.

3) Threat modeling: new public embeddings endpoint (product request)
- Context: product wants a higher-throughput public embeddings API with cheaper units for anonymized telemetry use-case.
- Primary concerns:
  - Data exfiltration: embeddings may be reversible for certain inputs; need classification on input types allowed.
  - Abuse: automated scraping of model to build proprietary corpora. Rate limiting + per-key quotas required.
  - Multi-tenant isolation: ensure accelerator pools for hosted API cannot be used to cross-correlate tenant KV caches.
- Decisions / proposed controls:
  - Enforce strict input policy: reject PII patterns and block file uploads until content-scan pipeline is available. (Action: Rachel, draft policy by 2026-03-21)
  - Implement per-key rate limits + adaptive throttling; require developer registration for elevated throughput. (Action: Marcus, design doc due 2026-03-18)
  - Add differential logging: redact raw inputs for public endpoint and retain only hash-based telemetry. (Action: Daniel + Aisha, prototype by 2026-03-25)
  - Consider offering a private-only embeddings plan for regulated customers (product conversation).

4) Operational notes / measurements
- False positive rate for secret scanner was ~12% last week; goal to reduce to <5% within 2 weeks. Aisha to run daily tuning and report metrics to #sec-alerts.
- Mean time to triage (MTTT) for critical vuln currently 8.2 hours; target <4h. Plan: on-call rotation tweak and automated triage enrichment (add repro hints from CI).

5) Action items (owner - due)
- Marcus: deploy WAF rule for SEC-421 and validate (2026-03-14)
- Daniel: hotfix to disable untrusted-deserialize flag and ship canary (2026-03-15)
- Rachel: confirm customer impact for deserializer change; coordinate communication if needed (2026-03-16)
- Sofia: schedule dependency upgrade for embedding worker and finish SEC-430 validation hardening (2026-03-20)
- Aisha: tune secrets detector thresholds and produce false-positive report (2026-03-18)
- Daniel + Aisha: prototype redacted telemetry for public embeddings (2026-03-25)

Notes to self / unresolved:
- Need to confirm whether deserializer is used by any internal batch jobs that run with elevated privileges (Aisha to check inventory).
- Should we add 'expiration' enforcement for all CI-generated tokens? Evaluate token lifetime policy next sync.

Next meeting: 2026-03-21 10:00 PT (weekly cadence)

References / Links:
- JIRA: SEC-421, SEC-430
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987
- Confluence: Threat model draft (pageId=12345678)

End of notes.
